scope: Additive audit of public Hero Banner defender behavior claims. It enables no patrol or defender behavior in Core.
game_version: Current public pages were consulted on 2026-09-21. None identifies a client build or supplies a complete standard Home Village Hero Banner behavior contract.

sources.title: About Heroes & Pets
facts: Defending Heroes patrol around their assigned Hero Banner and defend against enemy attacks.
The page gives no patrol radius, route, acquisition range, target priority, pursuit, return, respawn, collision, or timing value.

sources.title: I think my Warden owed the def Queen some DE.
facts: A commenter claims a 10-tile defensive search radius for Archer Queen, Grand Warden, and Minion Prince and 9 tiles for other Heroes.
The claim has no reproducible capture, patch identifier, or authoritative measurement.
sources.limitations: The page is a user discussion, predates the Dragon Duke, and cannot establish a current deterministic rule.

sources.title: Removed question on defending Hero behavior
facts: A commenter claims a defending Hero can pursue a target acquired near its Banner until the target is eliminated, then return.
The claim has no capture, measurement, target-selection rule, or current game-version identifier.
sources.limitations: The submission is removed and the retained comment is insufficient to define Core behavior.

rejected_inferences.rule: Implement 9-tile and 10-tile Hero Banner acquisition radii.
rejected_inferences.reason: The only discovered values are an unverified secondary claim with incomplete current-Hero coverage.

rejected_inferences.rule: Implement unlimited pursuit and return after a locked target dies.
rejected_inferences.reason: The secondary description omits target selection, acquisition, pathing, loss, retargeting, return destination, and tick-order contracts.

items: pursuit, target loss, retargeting, and return
respawn, collision, wall interaction, and deterministic tick ordering

conclusion: The source search confirms the existing primary patrol statement but finds no sufficient public specification for deterministic defensive Hero behavior. The secondary claims are retained as research leads only.
